messages:
jordan: Hey team — installing private agent in customer VPC. Installer fails when pulling model shards and pip wheels. I see TLS / SNI mismatches and some 403s. Can you confirm the minimal outbound allowlist we should request from infra so this can pull models and report telemetry?

jordan: here's the exact curl I ran and the output:
```bash
curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/shards/abc123 -o /dev/null
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.10.10.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake aborted: SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp' doesn't match target host 'model-registry.redwood.ai'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp' doesn't match target host 'model-registry.redwood.ai'
```

marie: thanks — looks like your network is doing TLS intercept / SNI rewrite. Two quick asks so we can give a minimal list: 1) can you paste the installer log lines around the error (we need the exact hostnames it tries to hit), and 2) do you have a transparent proxy that terminates TLS? If yes, we need SNI passthrough for Redwood hosts or certificate pinning exceptions.

jordan: installer log (redacted) showing attempts:
```
2026-06-12T14:02:12Z INFO pulling shard https://model-registry.redwood.ai/shards/abc123
2026-06-12T14:02:13Z WARN tls verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (possibly corp-proxy)
2026-06-12T14:02:13Z ERROR http GET failed: 403 from proxy.corp
2026-06-12T14:02:14Z INFO pip download wheel https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...
2026-06-12T14:02:15Z ERROR pip wheel fetch failed: SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp' doesn't match target host 'files.pythonhosted.org'
```

devon: We're seeing similar tickets — core recommendation is to allow TLS passthrough for specific hostnames that require end-to-end TLS (model registry, auth, telemetry, package registries, OCSP/CRL). If you cannot passthrough, you need to ensure the proxy serves certs that validate for those hosts (rare).

marie: minimal allowlist we usually ask customers to open (outbound TCP 443 unless noted):
- model-registry.redwood.ai : model shards + auth token exchange
- auth.redwood.ai : token issuance / refresh
- telemetry.redwood.ai (or telemetry.prod.redwood.ai) : metrics/heartbeat
- files.pythonhosted.org : pip wheels
- pypi.org : package metadata
- *.s3.amazonaws.com (or the specific region S3 host) : model shard storage (if using S3-backed registry)
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org and ocsp.identrust.com : OCSP stapling / revocation checks
- crl.identrust.com and crl.microsoft.com : CRL endpoints used by some distros
- cdn.jsdelivr.net and cdn.jsdelivr.com : some wheel/asset CDN mirrors
- fonts.gstatic.com (if GUI/console loads)
- repo.maven.org (if using Java deps)
- registry-1.docker.io and auth.docker.io : container image pulls (if installer pulls images)

marie: notes / ports / tips:
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS) is the rule of thumb. Some package managers may use 80 for redirects; allow 80->443 redirects.
- SNI passthrough: if your proxy does TLS terminate/inspect, configure passthrough for the exact hostnames above (wildcards ok for S3 buckets).
- If passthrough is not possible, the proxy must present certificates that are valid for the service hostnames (not common).
- For S3-backed shards: prefer allowing the specific regional S3 hostname to avoid cross-region issues.
- OCSP/CRL: allowlist the OCSP/CRL hosts so certificate validation works end-to-end (blocking these causes strange TLS failures).

infra-bot: automated check: we recommend also allowing outbound to the following IP ranges if your infra uses egress NAT and you need IP-based rules (better to use hostnames + SNI passthrough):
- 3.5.0.0/16 (example S3 range)
- 13.32.0.0/15 (CDN ranges)
(Your cloud provider has published current ranges; please sync with them.)

jordan: couple clarifying q's — telemetry: does it use HTTP or UDP? And does auth use a separate port?

marie: telemetry uses HTTPS (443) to telemetry.redwood.ai -> JSON posts. No UDP. Auth is standard HTTPS to auth.redwood.ai. No special ports.

marie: copy/paste minimal allowlist you can hand to infra (one-per-line):
model-registry.redwood.ai:443  # model shards + registry API
auth.redwood.ai:443            # token issuance / introspect
telemetry.redwood.ai:443      # metrics/heartbeat/events
files.pythonhosted.org:443     # pip wheels
pypi.org:443                  # pip metadata
*.s3.amazonaws.com:443        # model blobs (allow region-specific host if possible)
ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org:80,443  # OCSP checks (HTTP allowed)
ocsp.identrust.com:80,443
crl.identrust.com:80,443
cdn.jsdelivr.net:443
registry-1.docker.io:443
auth.docker.io:443
repo.maven.org:443

jordan: thanks — I'll ask infra to add SNI passthrough for that set and re-test. I'll report back the curl/installer logs once they make the change. Really appreciate the quick checklist :thumbsup:

jordan: update: infra enabled SNI passthrough for the hosts above, reran the installer, model shards now download cleanly and pip wheels install. All good on our side, thanks team! :tada:
